architectural_notes: Infra: a reporting artifact produced against real branch data as part of accepting the migration. The probe logic lives in app/services (the same parse rule used for backfill, reused to classify), reading rows via app/repositories, and returns the count of nonconforming rows for review. It is observability over the data-store state (NFR-F6-integrity-probe), not a UI or API endpoint, hence Infra rather than API. It fabricates nothing; it only counts codes that fail the delimiter parse.
given: a set of sprint-1 stock rows in which some inventory_codes are full location-batch-serial codes and some are nonconforming
when: the integrity probe is run as part of accepting the change
then: it surfaces the count of nonconforming rows (those whose code could not be parsed into batch and serial) for review before the change is accepted

independence.rationale: Earlier ACs assert what the migration does to the data; AC5 asserts a separate reporting artifact, the count of nonconforming rows, is produced for review. The backfill could behave correctly while no probe count is surfaced, so this fails independently.
